title: Adaptive rollback curator: cohort-aware SLO triggers combining latency, errors, token-cost, throughput
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Implement an adaptive rollback curator that synthesizes multiple SLO signals (p95 latency, client-facing error rate, per-request token cost, and throughput churn) and computes cohort-aware, dynamically tuned rollback triggers for canary/A-B/shadow rollouts. The curator should: 1) profile traffic cohorts (customer, region, route, model-size) and compute baseline SLO distributions per-cohort; 2) normalize token-cost signal to unit-economics so cost regressions surface without drowning latency/error signals; 3) apply smoothing and hysteresis to reduce noise for low-volume cohorts; 4) expose confidence scores and rollback rationale in Console for operator review; 5) integrate with existing rollouts API to auto-evacuate traffic or flip to fallback variants when triggers fire.

Non-goals: replacing human judgment for complex product regressions; building a full causal analysis pipeline (we will provide links to traces and diffs but not root-cause inference in this phase).

Approach: Use a Bayesian posterior window (adaptive window length based on throughput) per-cohort to estimate delta from baseline and compute a risk score combining magnitude and uncertainty. Provide two action bands: advisory (notify + annotation) and execution (auto-rollback). Tune thresholds with a calibration job that replays historical incidents and synthetic perturbations to compute expected false positive/negative rates across cohort sizes.
comments: 2026-02-21 — Kickoff: scoped spike to validate cohort definition heuristics (route + customer tier + model-size). Spike found high cardinality for route tags; agreed to use route-prefix hashing to reduce cohorts.

2026-02-27 — Prototype: implemented baseline sampler in staging metrics pipeline; initial posterior estimator using 5m windows. Observed false positives in low-volume cohorts where p95 stdev was large.

2026-03-02 — Design sync with PM/DS: decided to add throughput-based adaptive windowing (scale window from 5m to 60m depending on event rate) and to include token-cost normalization by computing cost-per-token delta relative to historical median.

2026-03-05 — Staging rollout: enabled advisory notifications for 10% of staging canaries. Example incident: PRD-431 (synthetic token-cost spike) generated advisory at 08:12 UTC; flagged as correct and triggered manual investigation. Logged learnings in Confluence.
2026-03-08 — Implementation: opened GitHub PR #5678 with curator service and Console UI annotations. Perf review noted one hot-path allocation; addressing in follow-up PR #5721.

2026-03-10 — Tuning: updated smoothing window from 5m->15m for cohorts under 100 qps to reduce churn. Running calibration job against last 6 months of rollouts to pick default thresholds that target <0.5% false-positive for cohorts >500 qps and <5% for cohorts <20 qps.
Action items: finalize security review, add audit logging hooks, wire up rollout policy editor to allow product teams to opt-in to execution band per-project.
acceptance_criteria: Curator service computes per-cohort risk score for latency, error rate, token-cost, throughput every minute and writes to metrics DB
Console shows advisory and execution bands with human-readable rationale and confidence score in rollout timeline

Auto-execution path can be toggled per-project; when enabled, a detected high-confidence execution band triggers automatic rollback to fallback model and creates a rollback event with full audit trail
False-positive rate in calibration tests below target thresholds for defined cohort buckets
Integration tests and load tests demonstrating curator adds <2% latency to rollout decision path under 2000 qps
steps: 1) Finish core curator algorithm and unit tests (Bayesian posterior estimator + adaptive windowing)
2) Wire curator into metrics pipeline (staging) and emit exploratory dashboards (Grafana) for manual validation
3) Implement Console annotations + rollout policy toggle UI
4) Run calibration job against historical rollouts + synth perturbations to select default thresholds
6) Staged canary: advisory-only for 2 weeks, then opt-in execution in safe small set of customers
7) Postmortem and TL;DR runbook for operators (how to override/triage curator decisions)
